Amkor $AMKR announced Phase 2 of its Arizona advanced packaging and test campus, adding 60,000 square meters of cleanroom capacity and raising planned investment to about $12 billion.

The Details:

•	Customer demand: Customer commitments exceeded the 33,000 square meters of cleanroom capacity planned for Phase 1.

•	Campus scale: Phase 2 would bring the campus to about 93,000 square meters of cleanroom space across wafer bump, probe, assembly, and test capabilities.

•	Construction timing: Amkor expects Phase 2 construction to begin in late 2027 and finish by the end of 2029.

•	Workforce impact: The combined phases are expected to support more than 3,500 Arizona-based employees.

GameStop $GME director Lawrence Cheng reported buying 55,000 Class A common shares on Sept. 8 at $18.7992 per share through Cheng Capital LLC.

The Details:

•	Transaction type: The filing reports an open-market purchase, identified by transaction code P.

•	Ownership total: Cheng beneficially owned 143,000 GameStop Class A common shares after the reported transaction.

•	Ownership form: The shares are held indirectly through Cheng Capital LLC.

•	Reporting role: Cheng is listed as a GameStop director and 10% owner in the filing.

Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon said Tuesday he is leaving the AI industry, citing concerns that companies are racing to build self-improving systems they cannot control.

The Details:

•	Departure rationale: Coxon said he does not want to contribute to systems he fears could improve themselves, evade human commands, and become uncontrollable.

•	Industry concerns: He said competitive pressure among AI companies and Chinese rivals makes safety trade-offs inevitable.

•	Anthropic stance: Coxon said Anthropic’s safety work is earnest, but argued no company can responsibly develop AI surpassing humans across tasks without intervention.

•	Policy request: Coxon joined more than 1,000 researchers urging international coordination for a development slowdown if controls become necessary.

Palantir $PLTR named Nebius $NBIS its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner, announcing a strategic partnership to integrate Nebius compute and inference endpoints directly inside Palantir’s enterprise perimeter. The integration will allow eligible Palantir commercial customers to run open AI models on Nebius infrastructure, continuously adapt them using proprietary company data, and maintain control over their compute, models, and data. The companies also plan to bring new AI compute capacity online faster, including modular data-center deployments in locations where power is already available.
